02 / Silent motion draft

A rate cut is not an automatic equity signal.

An educational mechanism using the explicitly dated June 2024 pilot.

24 seconds · 720 × 1280 · 9:16 · 24 fps · H.264 · No audio

Download MP4 ↓ Poster

Readable transcript

  1. 00–06s
    A rate cut. An equity rally?

    There is no automatic link.

    A question before a conclusion
    Graphic text: POLICY RATE: downward arrow. EQUITY INDEX: question mark. A mechanism is not a guarantee.
  2. 06–12s
    Two channels. Opposing forces.

    Lower rates can help valuations. Weak demand can hurt earnings.

    Trace the mechanism
    Graphic text: Lower financing costs → Can support valuations. Weaker demand → Can pressure earnings.
  3. 12–18s
    June 2024: different decisions.

    ECB cut. Fed held. That is a starting point, not a signal.

    A dated teaching case
    Graphic text: ECB: −25 bp; deposit rate → 3.75%. FED: HOLD; target → 5.25–5.50%. ECB 6 June / Fed 12 June 2024.
  4. 18–24s
    Ask why. Then ask what’s already priced in.

    Read the historical case. Test the explanation.

    The useful next question
    Graphic text: INFLATION. DEMAND. EARNINGS. Each receives a check mark.

Historical factual sources: ECB, 6 June 2024 and Federal Reserve, 12 June 2024. The mechanism is conditional analysis, not an observed return or causal price attribution.

03 / Silent motion draft

Slower inflation does not automatically mean falling prices.

An illustrative price-index example showing disinflation and deflation.

24 seconds · 720 × 1280 · 9:16 · 24 fps · H.264 · No audio

Download MP4 ↓ Poster

Readable transcript

  1. 00–06s
    Inflation falls. Do prices fall?

    Not automatically.

    Two ideas worth separating
    Graphic text: INFLATION RATE: downward arrow. PRICE LEVEL: question mark. A slower rise is still a rise.
  2. 06–12s
    Prices can rise more slowly.

    Illustrative price index: 100 → 110 → 115.5

    Watch the price level
    Graphic text: ILLUSTRATIVE PRICE INDEX. Base 100; Year 1:110; Year 2:115.5. The line rises, then rises more slowly.
  3. 12–18s
    From 10% to 5%: disinflation.

    Growth slows. The price level still rises.

    Give the change its name
    Graphic text: ILLUSTRATIVE PRICE INDEX. Base100; Year1:110, +10%; Year2:115.5, +5%.
  4. 18–24s
    Falling prices are deflation.

    Disinflation slows the increase. Deflation reverses the direction.

    A different direction
    Graphic text: ILLUSTRATIVE DIRECTIONS. DISINFLATION: price level rises at a slower pace. DEFLATION: downward arrow shows a falling price level.

All numeric material is an original arithmetic illustration: a base index of 100 rising 10% becomes 110; a further 5% rise becomes 115.5. The lines are conceptual, with no actual price data, forecast or implied performance.
